scope: Independent source review of deterministic method selection, release gate, execution grouping, and planned bootstrap; no prospective observation was generated or inspected by this review.

checks.detail: Both completed development datasets require the registered spec hash, expected records/cases/methods/replicates/seeds, a passed audit binding the current spec/summary/ledger, matching complete case definitions, and pinned algorithm sources.

The candidate is the lowest equal-case geometric mean unconditional cost among the three RB methods; the primary comparator is the lowest among the eighteen registered non-RB controls. Exact metric ties use ascending method name. All errors and cap abstentions remain in per-case mean costs. No development-superiority gate was added.

Selection, plan, algorithm sources, wrapper/analysis hashes and explicit root release are bound before run mode invokes a simulator. Selection and release modes themselves do not sample observations. Existing release, spec, ledger and completed analysis files are not overwritten.

The selected candidate, primary comparator and fixed PSR-beta secondary are deduplicated. Methods share independent case/replicate seed labels. Refined engines within one policy share observation prefixes while preserving their own first stopping costs; unequal protocols have separately reconstructed trajectories under the same labels.

The plan has 48 main cases times 64 replicates plus 8 null cases times 16 replicates, totaling 3200 independent joint labels. Main and null caps are kept distinct. Complete data and the exact expected method matrix are required for primary analysis; a cutoff does not authorize sample reduction or replacement.

The analysis uses 5000 RandomState(914207) resamples. Within each main case, 64 replicate labels are sampled with replacement and the identical index matrix is applied to every method; each case draws a new matrix. It recomputes case means and then the equal-case geometric mean of candidate/comparator ratios. Primary and secondary use the same resamples.

Linear-interpolated 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles match the plan. The primary numerical threshold requires the unrounded upper endpoint strictly below one. The analysis labels scientific acceptance as additionally requiring a passed independent audit; it does not silently convert the numerical flag to a scientific pass. The secondary remains descriptive.

The final analyze.py stores each row with records.append rather than repeated list concatenation. This performance edit does not change selection, resampling, statistics or acceptance. Its final hash is recorded above.

limits: This review does not execute or validate any prospective data; a full post-run implementation audit is still required.
The confidence intervals concern Monte Carlo uncertainty on the fixed case matrix, not uncertainty over a population of unseen problem instances.
Passing the registered comparison would establish a claim against the selected named implementation, not full-field SOTA dominance or theorem novelty.
The explicit-root-release condition is an operational instruction; a command-line reference string alone is not evidence of external user authorization.
